drivingQuestion: Why does the baraita require investigation specifically in the case of a child carrying a torch?
outcomeNote: Rav's restriction of the baraita to the hour after sunset explains why only a child is in question.

segments.he: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הָיָה מְהַלֵּךְ חוּץ לַכְּרַךְ וְרָאָה תִּינוֹק וַאֲבוּקָה בְּיָדוֹ, בּוֹדֵק אַחֲרָיו; אִם יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא — מְבָרֵךְ, אִם נָכְרִי הוּא — אֵינוֹ מְבָרֵךְ.
segments.en: And «the Sages taught: One who was walking outside the city» at the conclusion of Shabbat «and saw a child with a torch in his hand, he» must «check after his» background. «If» the child «is a Jew, he may recite a blessing» over this flame, «but if» the child «is a gentile, he may not recite a blessing» over it.

segments.he: מַאי אִירְיָא תִּינוֹק? אֲפִילּוּ גָּדוֹל נָמֵי!
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «Why was it taught» specifically with regard to «a child? Even if he were an adult,» one would «also» need to investigate whether he was a Jew or a gentile in order to determine whether or not he may recite a blessing over the torch.

segments.he: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: הָכָא בְּסָמוּךְ לִשְׁקִיעַת הַחַמָּה עָסְקִינַן. גָּדוֹל, מוֹכְחָא מִילְּתָא דְּוַדַּאי נָכְרִי הוּא. תִּינוֹק, אֵימַר יִשְׂרָאֵל הוּא, אִקְּרִי וּנְקֵיט.
segments.en: «Rav Yehuda said» that «Rav said: Here we are dealing with» a case where, although it was the conclusion of Shabbat, it was still «soon after sunset.» Therefore, in the case of «an adult, it is self-evident that he is a gentile,» as a Jew would not be so quick to take fire in his hand immediately after Shabbat. In the case of «a child,» however, «say that» perhaps «he is a Jew» and «it happened that he took» the torch.
